text:
ashley: Heads-up — noticed a spike in GPU OOMs in prod after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Rolling 0.9.3->0.9.4 landed on 3 clusters and two pods per cluster hit OOM within minutes :grimacing:
tyler: Which change in the selector? Was it the aggressive vectorized attention path for long ctx?
maria: I ran a quick diff — the selector now prefers fused attention kernel when seq_len>1024 and batch_size<4, and falls back otherwise. Looks fine but the fallback path changed batching heuristics (more small micro-batches getting promoted to contiguous KV allocations).
ashley: Repro logs attached from one pod: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:23:11Z] mem_total_gpu=40GB mem_free=2.8GB GPU_OOM at evict_shard: cannot allocate KV slab size=768MB
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] kv_cache_hit_rate=0.12 prefix_hitrate_window=5m
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] kernel_selected=fused_attention_v2 fallback=scalar_attn
```
kevin: That hit rate looks terrible. 12% prefix hit in steady traffic implies cold blast to GPU for most requests. Did rollout change keying semantics?
maria: We didn't touch keying, but the batching promotion logic now pads different numerical alignments which increases fragmentation in the GPU slab allocator. Small leftover holes stack up and compaction doesn't trigger until heavy pressure.
tyler: Could be two interacting things: kernel change increases per-request KV footprint (more segments kept), and batching heuristic reduces coalescing opportunities. Result: higher effective working set -> fragmentation -> OOMs.
ashley: Suggested immediate mitigation: 1) rollback kernel-selector for the two affected clusters, 2) tune eviction/TTL to more aggressive compact-on-free, 3) temporary increase GPU slab compaction frequency. Anyone object?
kevin: Rollback is safest. But we should also collect profiling (alloc/free sizes + slab histogram) before revert so we can compare. I can add a small flamegraph and slab histogram collector to the next deploy.
maria: For TTL tuning, I propose decreasing prefix TTL from 10m -> 2m for the small-key cohort (cohort=short prompts). That should shrink working set quickly and improve hit rate stability. Also enable proactive compaction when frag>0.25.
ashley: Agree. We should also add an opt-in experiment: A/B between current batching heuristic and a coalescing-first variant that delays small micro-batches for up to 5ms to let another request merge (only when p99 latency headroom allows).
tyler: Implementation note: introduce an adaptive delay window keyed by queue depth and route SLAs. If queue_depth<2 and tail_slo slack>10ms, delay up to 5ms. Otherwise immediate.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1987. Pager thresholds muted for rollback window.
kevin: For profiling, here's the quick patch I want to run as non-disruptive: sample allocation sizes every 100ms + record slab fragmentation ratio. Snippet: 
```
/metrics/kv_slab_alloc_samples{pod} += 1
/metrics/kv_slab_frag_ratio{pod} = free_bytes/total_bytes
```
maria: Also capture kernel-selection counters per request so we can see distribution: fused vs scalar vs quantized paths. Add `kernel_selector.choice` tag to trace spans.
ashley: Okay plan: 1) rollback selector in 1h, 2) deploy frag sampler immediately to one canary node, 3) run TTL tweak config on canary, 4) run 5% A/B coalescing-delay. We'll reconvene after 2h of telemetry.
tyler: One more thought — fallback kernels can have different memory layout for KV (interleaved vs contiguous). We should ensure fallback maps to same allocation class to avoid cross-layout fragmentation. Opened GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3967
kevin: Adding link to the OOM heap dump: s3://prod-dumps/1951234567/oom-dump-1.tar.gz
maria: Quick diff of metrics after a 10m test on canary (simulated traffic): hit_rate went 0.11 -> 0.28 with TTL reduced + compaction tweak. GPU mem tail reduced from 95th=38GB->95th=33GB. Not perfect but promising.
nashley: Nice. If the rollback buys time we should still land the compaction heuristic and the batching A/B — those look like permanent improvements.
kevin: Agree. I'll coordinate a postmortem draft and include the slab histograms + kernel-selector distribution.
nashley: Thanks team. Will post updates in the thread during rollback. :thumbsup:
